subject: Negative factor loadings in CFA after excluding one item

messages.author: 7b9bcd1eccdbfdea
messages.subject: Negative factor loadings in CFA after excluding one item
parts:
Hi,

I am conducting a CFA with twelve items that are categorical. I received positive signs for the factor loadings in the CFA.

After I excluded one item which was problematic, all factor loadings switch from positive to negative.

Does anybody know why that is and how to handle it?

Thank you
Pascal

messages.author: 7b9bcd1eccdbfdea
messages.subject: Re: Negative factor loadings in CFA after excluding one item
parts:
It would be really important for us to have positive factor loadings for the interpretability of our results. So I tried the following approach:

model <- 'Construct =~  a * item1 + b* item2 + c * item3+ d*item4 + e*item5 + f*item7 + g *item8 + h*  item9 + i * item10 + j* item11 +  k* item13

a > 0
b > 0
c > 0
d > 0
e > 0
f > 0
g > 0
h > 0
i > 0
j > 0
k> 0
'

After doing this, I get exactly the same factor loadings in the CFA but with positive signs. Also, the model fit remains exactly the same.

Do you think this is a reasonable approach?

Thanks,
Pascal

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Negative factor loadings in CFA after excluding one item
parts: That is a tedious way to do it. The model as specified is indeterminate with respect to sign for the loadings. If only one is forced positive, then all will be estimated positive. Even just a single positive starting value would do the trick.
